correctness.rationale: Independence across disjoint species groups gives Var(Y)=∑(q^{s_i}−q^{2s_i}). Algebraic differencing proves exact per-transfer factorization; its positive first two factors reduce sign to monotone q-map (1+q)(q^a+q^{b−1}). For all a≥1,b−1≥2 the quantity is bounded above by q(1+q)^2, yielding universal minimizing balanced profiles up to unique rho≈0.465571; a=1,b=3 attains the bound and reverses above rho. High-q fixed-S sufficient condition and same (S=9,F=3,q=1/2) opposite variance responses follow from the same identity. Independently checked rational identities and both nine-species contrasts; code CHECK.py uses separate direct 2^S loss enumeration for bounded cases.
residual_risks: At q=rho extra ties may occur; theorem does not claim global uniqueness at the equality boundary. High-q sufficient condition is not necessary.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Nijs–Impens introduced reliability of ecological functions under random independent loss. Fonseca–Ganade explicitly examine richness and variance under fixed-number species removals, a distinct dependent sampling model. Their established model does not imply this sharp uniform Bernoulli variance-balancing threshold. Hazra–Finkelstein–Cha compare whole-system series/parallel stochastic orders rather than variance of surviving independent subgroups.

value.rationale: Variance of surviving ecological functions is a natural independent uncertainty metric distinct from expected surviving functions. The exact sharp probability below which any balancing reduces variance, and the same-budget variance reversals above it, supply a complete meaningful parameter classification beyond re-deriving the textbook Bernoulli formula.
residual_risks: Model omits correlated failures and overlapping functions; fixed-count sampling results do not transfer mechanically.
